explanation: The name of the Christian savior who, according to Matthew 28, rose from the dead.
The event where Jesus left the tomb alive, confirming his divine nature and victory over death.
A heavenly messenger who in the text removes the stone from the tomb entrance and announces the resurrection to the women.
The place where Jesus was laid after crucifixion, now empty due to his resurrection.
A feeling of deep reverent fear mixed with joy that the women experienced when they met the angel at the tomb.
The action where the disciples set out to meet Jesus in Galilee, according to his own command.
One of the regions in ancient Israel where Jesus carried out his ministry and where he ordered his followers to meet him.
The ritual where disciples receive new believers by immersing them in water, as a sign of purity and new birth.
The first person of the Trinity, God the Almighty Creator, whose name is mentioned together with that of the Son and the Holy Spirit.
The second person of the Trinity, Jesus Christ himself, who shares the same essence as the Father.
The third person of the Trinity, God's Spirit who guides and strengthens believers after Jesus' ascension.
The command to teach disciples everything Jesus has taught them, including his words and deeds.
The invisible forces or angels present as witnesses when Jesus declares his authority over all things.
The term for the undisputed authority Jesus has received from the Father, covering both heaven and earth.
